subproblems.title: Mass lower bound for a current with a measure representation (printed (1) of Simon 3.13)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let Y ∈ D_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k), let μ be a measure on ℝ^N and κ : ℝ^N → Λ_k(ℝ^N) a field of k-vectors (NVector (Eucl N) k) such that (μ, κ) represents Y (IsMeasureRepresentation Y μ κ): for every test form ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^N) the function x ↦ κ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and Y(ω) = ∫ κ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). Then ∫ |κ(x)| dμ(x) ≤ M(Y) in [0, ∞], where |w| := (Σ_γ w(dx^γ)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean norm of a k-vector w (w(dx^γ) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate w γ, dx^γ = wedgeCovectors k (proj ∘ γ), γ ranging over the strictly increasing multi-indices SimonMultiIndex k N) and M(Y) = Y.mass = Y.massOn univ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: printed display (1) of Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 (M_W(T_Q − T_P) ≥ ∫_W |θ_Pξ_P − θ_Qξ_Q| dHⁿ), i.e. the lower half of the mass formula M(T) = ∫|T⃗| dμ_T of Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8. This is the Lemma of Step 2 of the parent proof (λ′ := μ, κ := κ), stated for an arbitrary measure representation, and its argument is followed: restrict to a ball, choose a continuous field of norm ≤ 1 that is close to κ/|κ| on most of the |κ|-mass, cut it off, mollify it into a test form and rescale it into the admissible class. The parent proof obtains the continuous field from inner regularity, Lusin's theorem and Tietze's theorem. Those two theorems are not in the frozen import closure (Mathlib.Topology.TietzeExtension, Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense and SimonGMT Chapter01.Lusin are not imported by GMT/Ch06/Contract.lean). Steps 4–6 below therefore produce the same estimate ν(ℝ^N) − O(ε) through the elementary density of continuous compactly supported maps in L¹ of a finite Borel measure, which is proved in Step 4 from regularity and Urysohn's lemma (the usual proof of Lusin's theorem). The hypothesis IsMeasureRepresentation replaces "λ′ locally finite and κ λ′-integrable on bounded sets"; Step 1 derives the local integrability that is needed.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ i. I := SimonMultiIndex k N (order embeddings γ : Fin k ↪o Fin N, i.e. strictly increasing γ), m := #I. For γ ∈ I: e_γ := (e_{γ(0)}, …, e_{γ(k−1)}) and dx^γ := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (γ j)). For a k-covector α: α_γ := α(e_γ) = euclideanCovectorCoordinate α γ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, and ‖α‖ is its operator norm. For a k-vector w: w^γ := w(dx^γ) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate w γ, c(w) := (w^γ)_γ ∈ ℝ^I := EuclideanSpace ℝ I, and |w| := ‖c(w)‖ = (Σ_γ (w^γ)²)^{1/2}. ‖·‖ and ⟨·,·⟩ on ℝ^I are Euclidean. B_R := ball 0 R, B̄_R := closedBall 0 R, h(x) := |κ(x)|. M := M(Y) = Y.mass = Y.massOn univ.

0. Linear algebra.
 (a) (Pairing; sibling pairing_expansion.) w(α) = Σ_γ α_γ w^γ for every k-vector w and k-covector α, and |α_γ| ≤ |α|.
 (b) |α|² = Σ_γ α_γ². Indeed covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin N} [J strictly increasing] α(basisFun ∘ J)²)^{1/2}; the strictly increasing J correspond bijectively to the γ ∈ I (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono, and the coercion of an order embedding to a strictly increasing map), and basisFun (J i) = e_{J i}. So |α| is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector (α_γ)_γ ∈ ℝ^I. In particular |s·α| = |s|·|α| for s ∈ ℝ.
 (c) (Cauchy–Schwarz.) By (a), (b) and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^I, |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w|.
 (d) (Kronecker.) For γ, β ∈ I, dx^γ(e_β) = 1 if γ = β and 0 otherwise. By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^γ(e_β) = det[δ_{γ(i), β(j)}]_{i,j}. For γ = β this is det 1 = 1. For γ ≠ β the ranges differ, because a strictly increasing map is determined by its range; both ranges have k elements, so some γ(i) ∉ range β, row i of the matrix is zero, and the determinant is 0.
 (e) For a ∈ ℝ^I let a♭ := Σ_γ a_γ dx^γ, a k-covector depending linearly (hence continuously) on a. By (d), (a♭)_β = a_β. Hence |a♭| = ‖a‖ by (b), and w(a♭) = Σ_γ a_γ w^γ = ⟨a, c(w)⟩ by (a).
 (f) (Radial retraction.) For a ∈ ℝ^I let π(a) := a / max{1, ‖a‖}. Then π is continuous, ‖π(a)‖ ≤ 1, and π(a) = a when ‖a‖ ≤ 1. Moreover ‖π(a) − b‖ ≤ ‖a − b‖ whenever ‖b‖ ≤ 1. This is trivial if ‖a‖ ≤ 1. If t := ‖a‖ > 1, then ‖a − b‖² − ‖a/t − b‖² = t² − 1 − 2(1 − 1/t)⟨a, b⟩ ≥ t² − 1 − 2(1 − 1/t)·t = (t − 1)² ≥ 0, using ⟨a, b⟩ ≤ ‖a‖‖b‖ ≤ t.

1. (Local integrability of the coordinates.) Let R > 0 and choose a C^∞ function φ_R : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with compact support and φ_R = 1 on B̄_R (a smooth bump function, e.g. ContDiffBump or exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset). For γ ∈ I the form x ↦ φ_R(x) • dx^γ is smooth with compact support, hence an element of TestFormOn univ k. By hypothesis x ↦ κ(x)(φ_R(x) • dx^γ) = φ_R(x)κ^γ(x) is μ-integrable. As φ_R = 1 on B̄_R, κ^γ is μ-integrable on B̄_R. Hence h = ‖(κ^γ)_γ‖ ≤ Σ_γ |κ^γ| is μ-integrable on B̄_R; put C_R := ∫_{B̄_R} h dμ < ∞. Each κ^γ, hence h, is μ-a.e. strongly measurable on every B̄_R, hence on ℝ^N = ⋃_{R ∈ ℕ} B̄_R.

2. (Continuous competitors.) Claim: let R > 0 and let f : ℝ^N → Λ^k(ℝ^N) be continuous, with tsupport f compact and contained in B_R, and |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then x ↦ κ(x)(f(x)) is μ-integrable, and if M < ∞ then ∫ κ(x)(f(x)) dμ ≤ M.toReal.
 (a) Integrability. By 0(a), κ(x)(f(x)) = Σ_γ f(x)_γ κ^γ(x). Each f_γ is continuous, |f_γ| ≤ 1 by 0(b), and f_γ = 0 off B̄_R, while κ^γ is μ-integrable on B̄_R (Step 1).
 (b) Smoothing. Since tsupport f is a compact subset of the open ball B_R, there is d > 0 such that the closed d-thickening of tsupport f is still contained in B_R (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open; this also covers tsupport f = ∅ and N = 0). Let δ ∈ (0, 1). Every k-covector satisfies |α| ≤ c‖α‖ with c := √m + 1, since |α_γ| = |α(e_γ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j ‖e_{γ(j)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). f is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support), so choose σ ∈ (0, d) with ‖f(x) − f(y)‖ ≤ δ/c whenever |x − y| < σ. Let ψ : ℝ^N → [0, ∞) be C^∞ with support in the ball B_σ(0) and ∫ψ = 1 (a smooth bump with compact support in B_σ(0), divided by its positive integral). Put η := ψ ⋆ f (convolution: η(x) = ∫ψ(y) f(x − y) dy). Then η is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), its support lies in tsupport f + B_σ(0), so tsupport η lies in the closed σ-thickening of tsupport f, hence is compact and contained in B_R, and ‖η(x) − f(x)‖ ≤ δ/c for every x (dist_convolution_le). Hence |η(x) − f(x)| ≤ δ for every x, and η is a test form, η ∈ TestFormOn univ k.
 (c) If M = ∞ there is nothing to prove; let M < ∞. By (b) and 0(b), |η(x)| ≤ 1 + δ. So η′ := (1 + δ)⁻¹ • η is a test form with tsupport η′ ⊆ univ and |η′(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, i.e. η′ ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ. GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η′)) ≤ Y.massOn univ = M, so Y(η′) ≤ M.toReal, i.e. Y(η) ≤ (1 + δ)M.toReal.
 (d) Y(η) = ∫ κ(η) dμ by the representation. By 0(c), and since η − f vanishes off B_R, |∫ κ(η) dμ − ∫ κ(f) dμ| ≤ ∫_{B̄_R} h·|η − f| dμ ≤ δ·C_R. Hence ∫ κ(f) dμ ≤ (1 + δ)M.toReal + δC_R. Letting δ ↓ 0 gives ∫ κ(f) dμ ≤ M.toReal.

3. (The finite measure ν and the polar field.) Fix R > 0 and ε > 0. By Step 1 choose Borel functions κ̃^γ with κ̃^γ = κ^γ μ-a.e. on B̄_R. Put h̃ := ‖(κ̃^γ)_γ‖ (Borel), Z := {x ∈ B_R : h̃(x) > 0} (Borel), and let u : ℝ^N → ℝ^I be u(x) := (κ̃^γ(x)/h̃(x))_γ for x ∈ Z and u(x) := 0 otherwise. Then u is Borel, ‖u‖ ≤ 1 everywhere and ‖u‖ = 1 on Z. Let ν := (μ⌞B_R).withDensity h̃, i.e. ν(A) = ∫_{A ∩ B_R} h̃ dμ for Borel A. ν is a finite Borel measure: ν(ℝ^N) = ∫_{B_R} h dμ ≤ C_R. Also ν(ℝ^N ∖ Z) = 0. Finally c(κ(x)) = h̃(x)u(x) for μ-a.e. x ∈ B_R: where h̃(x) > 0 this is c(κ̃(x)) = c(κ(x)), and where h̃(x) = 0 both sides vanish (c(κ̃(x)) = 0 and κ^γ = κ̃^γ a.e.).

4. (Continuous approximation.) Claim: there is a continuous map g₀ : ℝ^N → ℝ^I with compact support and ∫ ‖g₀ − u‖ dν < ε.
 (a) u is Borel and bounded and ν is finite, so u ∈ L¹(ν; ℝ^I).
 (b) Indicators. Let t ⊆ ℝ^N be Borel, a ∈ ℝ^I and ϵ > 0. A finite Borel measure on ℝ^N is inner regular with respect to compact sets and outer regular with respect to open sets (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_isClosed_sdiff_lt, MeasurableSet.exists_isOpen_sdiff_lt). So there are a compact s ⊆ t with ν(t ∖ s) < ϵ and an open V ⊇ s with ν(V ∖ s) < ϵ. Intersecting V with a relatively compact open neighbourhood of s, we may assume closure V is compact. By Urysohn's lemma (exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed) there is a continuous φ : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with φ = 1 on s and φ = 0 off V. Then φ·a is continuous with compact support, and ∫ ‖φa − 1_t a‖ dν ≤ ‖a‖·(ν(V ∖ s) + ν(t ∖ s)) < 2‖a‖ϵ, because φa − 1_t a vanishes on s and off V ∪ t and has norm ≤ ‖a‖.
 (c) Simple functions Σ_i 1_{t_i} a_i (finitely many Borel t_i) are dense in L¹(ν; ℝ^I) (MemLp.induction_dense, or the standard approximation of integrable functions by simple functions). Approximating u within ε/2 by such a simple function, and each of its finitely many terms within ε/(2·#terms) by (b), gives g₀ by the triangle inequality.

subproblems.title: Almost-everywhere and L¹ limit of a sequence with summable L¹ increments (Riesz–Fischer)
subproblems.statement: Let X be a type with a σ-algebra and a measure μ, let E be a complete normed additive group, and let f_n : X → E (n ∈ ℕ) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with Σ_n ∫‖f_{n+1} − f_n‖ dμ < ∞ (the sum of the [0, ∞]-valued lintegrals of the extended norms ‖f_{n+1}(x) − f_n(x)‖ₑ is ≠ ∞). Then there is a μ-a.e. strongly measurable g : X → E such that f_n(x) → g(x) for μ-a.e. x and ∫‖f_n − g‖ dμ → 0 as n → ∞ (lintegrals of ‖f_n(x) − g(x)‖ₑ in [0, ∞]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℕ → X → E), (∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (f n) μ) → (∑' n, ∫⁻ x, ‖f (n + 1) x - f n x‖ₑ ∂μ) ≠ ∞ → ∃ g : X → E, AEStronglyMeasurable g μ ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 (g x))) ∧ Tendsto (fun n => ∫⁻ x, ‖f n x - g x‖ₑ ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof (printed (2)–(3) of Simon 3.13): "the series κ₁ + Σ_j(κ_{j+1} − κ_j) … converge λ-a.e. (absolutely) to functions κ, θ, with ∫|κ_j − κ|dλ ≤ Σ_{i≥j}∫|κ_{i+1} − κ_i|dλ → 0 … (only the differences need to be integrable)". Here this classical Riesz–Fischer argument is stated for an arbitrary measure (no σ-finiteness) and an arbitrary complete normed group; the parent applies it to the coordinate vectors of the k-vector densities, with values in EuclideanSpace ℝ (SimonMultiIndex k N).

1. (Increments.) Put d_n(x) := ‖f_{n+1}(x) − f_n(x)‖ₑ ∈ [0, ∞]. Since f_{n+1} − f_n is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, d_n is μ-a.e. measurable. Let S(x) := Σ_n d_n(x) ∈ [0, ∞]. By the monotone convergence theorem for series of nonnegative a.e.-measurable functions (lintegral_tsum), ∫⁻ S dμ = Σ_n ∫⁻ d_n dμ < ∞ by hypothesis. Hence S(x) < ∞ for μ-a.e. x (ae_lt_top).

2. (Pointwise Cauchy property.) Fix x with S(x) < ∞ and put T_n(x) := Σ_{i≥n} d_i(x). For m ≥ n the triangle inequality gives ‖f_m(x) − f_n(x)‖ₑ ≤ Σ_{i=n}^{m−1} d_i(x) ≤ T_n(x), and T_n(x) → 0 as n → ∞, being the tails of a series with finite sum S(x) (ENNReal.tendsto_sum_nat_add). So (f_n(x))_n is a Cauchy sequence in the complete space E and converges.

3. (The limit g.) Define g(x) := lim_n f_n(x) when this limit exists and g(x) := 0 otherwise (e.g. g(x) := limUnder atTop (fun n ↦ f_n(x)) when the sequence converges). By Steps 1–2, f_n(x) → g(x) for μ-a.e. x. Being a μ-a.e. limit of μ-a.e. strongly measurable functions (the filter atTop on ℕ is countably generated), g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae).

4. (Tail bound.) Let x be as in Step 2 and n ∈ ℕ. Since f_m(x) → g(x) and ‖·‖ₑ is continuous, ‖f_n(x) − g(x)‖ₑ = lim_m ‖f_n(x) − f_m(x)‖ₑ ≤ T_n(x) by Step 2. Hence ‖f_n − g‖ₑ ≤ T_n μ-a.e.

5. (L¹ convergence.) By Step 4, monotonicity of the lintegral and lintegral_tsum, ∫⁻ ‖f_n − g‖ₑ dμ ≤ ∫⁻ T_n dμ = Σ_{i≥n} ∫⁻ d_i dμ. The right side is the n-th tail of the series Σ_i ∫⁻ d_i dμ, whose sum is finite, so it tends to 0 as n → ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_sum_nat_add). Hence ∫⁻ ‖f_n − g‖ₑ dμ → 0. Together with Step 3 this proves the statement. ∎

Formalization note. The following Lean proof of exactly this declaration compiles against the frozen commit d8d46c9 (lake env lean in the comparator scope, default maxHeartbeats, no set_option, no sorry; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). It follows Steps 1–5: lintegral_tsum and ae_lt_top' (Step 1), cauchySeq_of_edist_le_of_tsum_ne_top (Step 2), limUnder and aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae (Step 3), edist_le_tsum_of_edist_le_of_tendsto (Step 4), ENNReal.tendsto_sum_nat_add (Step 5).

```lean
theorem Submission.imc_ae_tendsto_of_summable_lintegral :
    ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℕ → X → E), (∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (f n) μ) → (∑' n, ∫⁻ x, ‖f (n + 1) x - f n x‖ₑ ∂μ) ≠ ∞ → ∃ g : X → E, AEStronglyMeasurable g μ ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 (g x))) ∧ Tendsto (fun n => ∫⁻ x, ‖f n x - g x‖ₑ ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  intro X _ μ E _ _ f hf hsum
  set d : ℕ → X → ℝ≥0∞ := fun n x => ‖f (n + 1) x - f n x‖ₑ with hd_def
  have hd : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (d n) μ := fun n => ((hf (n + 1)).sub (hf n)).enorm
  have hS : ∫⁻ x, ∑' n, d n x ∂μ = ∑' n, ∫⁻ x, d n x ∂μ := lintegral_tsum hd
  have hfin : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∑' n, d n x < ∞ :=
    ae_lt_top' (AEMeasurable.tsum hd) (by rw [hS]; exact hsum)
  have hedist : ∀ x n, edist (f n x) (f (n + 1) x) ≤ d n x := fun x n => by
    rw [edist_comm, edist_eq_enorm_sub]
  have hcauchy : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, CauchySeq (fun n => f n x) := by
    filter_upwards [hfin] with x hx
    exact cauchySeq_of_edist_le_of_tsum_ne_top (fun n => d n x) (hedist x) hx.ne
  set g : X → E := fun x => limUnder atTop (fun n => f n x) with hg_def
  have hlim : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 (g x)) := by
    filter_upwards [hcauchy] with x hx
    exact hx.tendsto_limUnder
  refine ⟨g, aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae atTop hf hlim, hlim, ?_⟩
  have htail : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f n x - g x‖ₑ ≤ ∑' m, d (n + m) x := by
    intro n
    filter_upwards [hfin, hlim] with x hx hxl
    rw [← edist_eq_enorm_sub]
    exact edist_le_tsum_of_edist_le_of_tendsto (fun m => d m x) (hedist x) hxl n
  have hbound : ∀ n, ∫⁻ x, ‖f n x - g x‖ₑ ∂μ ≤ ∑' m, ∫⁻ x, d (n + m) x ∂μ := by
    intro n
    calc ∫⁻ x, ‖f n x - g x‖ₑ ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x, ∑' m, d (n + m) x ∂μ := lintegral_mono_ae (htail n)
      _ = ∑' m, ∫⁻ x, d (n + m) x ∂μ := lintegral_tsum fun m => hd (n + m)
  have htend : Tendsto (fun n => ∑' m, ∫⁻ x, d (n + m) x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    have := ENNReal.tendsto_sum_nat_add (fun m => ∫⁻ x, d m x ∂μ) hsum
    simpa [add_comm] using this
  exact tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds htend (fun n => bot_le) hbound
```
proof_key_steps: ∫⁻ Σ_n ‖f_{n+1} − f_n‖ₑ = Σ_n ∫⁻ ‖f_{n+1} − f_n‖ₑ < ∞ (lintegral_tsum), so the increment series converges μ-a.e.
Where it converges, (f_n(x)) is Cauchy; completeness of E gives g(x); g is a.e. strongly measurable as an a.e. limit.
‖f_n − g‖ₑ ≤ Σ_{i≥n} ‖f_{i+1} − f_i‖ₑ a.e.; integrating, ∫⁻‖f_n − g‖ₑ is bounded by the vanishing tail of a convergent series.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent spaces of a subset agree a.e. with those of a locally finite superset (Lemma A)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[k] on ℝ^N, and let E ⊆ E′ ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable sets with H(E′ ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Then for H-a.e. x ∈ E (that is, H⌞E-a.e.) and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^N: Q is the approximate tangent space of E at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q: finrank Q = k and ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f dH → ∫_Q f dH as r → 0+ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x)) if and only if Q is the approximate tangent space of E′ at x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma A (locality) of Step 5 of the parent proof, unweighted half; Step 6 of the parent proof uses exactly this half (chain "Lemma B, Lemma A (twice), Lemma B"). The Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2)) it invokes is the sibling zero_density (imc_ae_zero_density_off_set, the case W = ℝ^N of the comparator-accepted lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set), and the dilation identity ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} g dH = r^{−k}∫_S g∘η_{x,r} dH is the comparator-accepted sibling blowup_cov (lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image).

Notation. H := μHE[k]; η_{x,r} := blowUpMap x r, η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x); B̄_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ. For a set S, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and r > 0 put I_S(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dH. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k S x Q means: finrank Q = k and I_S(r) → ∫_Q f dH as r → 0+ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N).

1. (Density zero of E′ ∖ E at points of E.) S := E′ ∖ E is H-null-measurable, and for every compact K, ∫⁻_{S∩K} 1 dH = H(S ∩ K) ≤ H(E′ ∩ K) < ∞. The sibling zero_density (imc_ae_zero_density_off_set), applied with Q := N, n := k, S := E′ ∖ E and g := 1, gives: for H-a.e. y with y ∉ E′ ∖ E, H((E′ ∖ E) ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) / ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^k) → 0 as ρ → 0+. Every y ∈ E satisfies y ∉ E′ ∖ E, so this holds for H-a.e. y ∈ E; an H-a.e. property restricted to E holds H⌞E-a.e. Let x ∈ E be such a point; the exceptional set does not depend on Q or f.

2. (Change of variables.) Fix such an x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N); choose R > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0) and let ‖f‖_∞ := sup |f|. For r > 0 put η := η_{x,r}. By blowup_cov (with Q := N, n := k, y := x, S := E, resp. S := E′, g := f), I_E(r) = r^{−k}∫_E f(η(z)) dH(z) and I_{E′}(r) = r^{−k}∫_{E′} f(η(z)) dH(z).

3. (Comparison.) The function z ↦ f(η(z)) is continuous, bounded by ‖f‖_∞ and vanishes unless ‖z − x‖ ≤ Rr, i.e. off the compact ball B̄_{Rr}(x). Since H(E′ ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) < ∞, f∘η is H-integrable on E′, on E and on E′ ∖ E. As E′ is the disjoint union of the H-null-measurable sets E and E′ ∖ E, ∫_{E′} f∘η dH = ∫_E f∘η dH + ∫_{E′∖E} f∘η dH. Therefore
 |I_{E′}(r) − I_E(r)| = r^{−k}|∫_{E′∖E} f∘η dH| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ r^{−k} H((E′ ∖ E) ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) = ‖f‖_∞ R^k · H((E′ ∖ E) ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) / (Rr)^k,
 which tends to 0 as r → 0+ by Step 1 (with ρ = Rr → 0+; all quantities are finite by local finiteness). Hence I_{E′}(r) − I_E(r) → 0 as r → 0+.

4. (Conclusion.) For x as in Step 1 and every subspace Q, the dimension conditions finrank Q = k of the two predicates coincide, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), I_E(r) → ∫_Q f dH if and only if I_{E′}(r) → ∫_Q f dH, by Step 3. Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E′ x Q for H⌞E-a.e. x, simultaneously for all Q. ∎

The blow-up integrals of E and E′ have the same limits for every f, so the approximate tangent spaces coincide for all Q.

It uses the siblings lusin_pieces (lpf_wtc_lusin_compact_pieces, comparator-accepted), zero_density (imc_ae_zero_density_off_set) and blowup_cov (lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image, comparator-accepted).

For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and r > 0: I_u(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f dH and I_w(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y). Since θ|C is continuous at x, for every ε′ > 0 there is s(ε′) > 0 with |θ(z) − θ(x)| ≤ ε′ for all z ∈ C ∩ B̄_{s(ε′)}(x); in particular θ ≥ θ(x)/2 on C ∩ B̄_{s₁}(x), where s₁ := s(θ(x)/2).
 Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), R > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0), and ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|; put D(r) := r^{−k}H(C ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) for r > 0. For r > 0, z ↦ f(η_{x,r}(z)) is bounded by ‖f‖_∞ and vanishes off B̄_{Rr}(x); as H(E ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) < ∞ and θ is integrable on E ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x), all integrals below are finite, and E is the disjoint union of the null-measurable sets C and S. Splitting the integrals of Step 1 accordingly:
 (a′) |r^{−k}∫_S f(η(z))θ(z) dH| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ R^k (∫_{S∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} θ dH)/(Rr)^k → 0 (θ > 0 on S; Step 3(b));
 (b′) |r^{−k}∫_S f(η(z)) dH| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ R^k H(S ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x))/(Rr)^k → 0 (Step 3(a));
 (c′) for Rr ≤ s(ε′): |r^{−k}∫_C f(η(z))(θ(z) − θ(x)) dH| ≤ ε′‖f‖_∞ D(r).
 Since I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r) = r^{−k}∫_C f(η)(θ − θ(x)) dH + r^{−k}∫_S f(η)θ dH − θ(x)r^{−k}∫_S f(η) dH, we get |I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r)| ≤ o(1) + ε′‖f‖_∞ D(r) for Rr ≤ s(ε′).

5. (D is bounded under either hypothesis.) Let g_R(y) := max{0, min{1, R + 1 − ‖y‖}}; g_R ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), 0 ≤ g_R ≤ 1, g_R = 1 on B̄_R(0), so g_R(η_{x,r}(z)) = 1 for z ∈ B̄_{Rr}(x).
 - If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q: by Step 1 (with g_R in place of f), D(r) ≤ r^{−k}∫_E g_R(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} g_R dH → ∫_Q g_R dH, so D(r) ≤ ∫_Q g_R dH + 1 for all small r > 0.
 - If HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q: for Rr ≤ s₁, as g_R ≥ 0 and θ > 0 on E, Step 1 gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} g_R(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) = r^{−k}∫_E g_R(η(z))θ(z) dH(z) ≥ r^{−k}∫_{C∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} θ dH ≥ (θ(x)/2)·D(r); the left side tends to θ(x)∫_Q g_R dH, so D(r) ≤ 2(θ(x)∫_Q g_R dH + 1)/θ(x) for all small r > 0.
 In both cases there are D₀ < ∞ and r₀ > 0 with D(r) ≤ D₀ for 0 < r < r₀.

6. (Comparison.) Assume either hypothesis and let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), ε″ > 0. Choose ε′ > 0 with ε′‖f‖_∞ D₀ < ε″; by Steps 4 and 5, |I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r)| < 2ε″ for all sufficiently small r > 0. Hence I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r) → 0 as r → 0+, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N).

7. (Conclusion.) Let x ∈ G and Q a subspace. (⇐) If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q, then for every f, I_u(r) → ∫_Q f dH and by Step 6 I_w(r) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH; with finrank Q = k this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q. (⇒) If HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q, then by Step 6 θ(x)I_u(r) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH for every f, and θ(x) > 0 gives I_u(r) → ∫_Q f dH; with finrank Q = k this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q. Since H⌞E-a.e. x lies in G (Step 3), the equivalence holds H⌞E-a.e., for all Q simultaneously. ∎

Lusin pieces C_i ⊆ E with θ|C_i continuous and H(E∖⋃C_i) = 0; zero_density gives density 0 of H⌞(E∖C_i) and θH⌞(E∖C_i) at a.e. point of C_i.
At such x: I_w(r) − θ(x)I_u(r) = o(1) + O(ε′·r^{−k}H(C_i ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x))) by continuity of θ|C_i.
r^{−k}H(C_i ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)) stays bounded under either hypothesis (test with g_R; θ ≥ θ(x)/2 near x on C_i).

subproblems.title: Pointwise eventual limits of rectifiable triples are rectifiable triples (orientation of the limit in Simon 3.13)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[k] on ℝ^N. For every j ∈ ℕ let (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple ℝ^N k M_j θ_j ξ_j with θ_j ≥ 1 on M_j. Let M₀ ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable, θ₀ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ₀ ≥ 1 on M₀ and θ₀ H-integrable on M₀ ∩ K for every compact K, and ξ₀ : ℝ^N → Λ_k(ℝ^N) (NVector). Assume that for H-a.e. x ∈ M₀ (H⌞M₀-a.e.) x ∈ M_j for all sufficiently large j and ξ_j(x) → ξ₀(x). Then IsRectifiableTriple ℝ^N k M₀ θ₀ ξ₀: M₀ is countably k-rectifiable, θ₀ > 0 on M₀ and locally H-integrable, ξ₀ is H⌞M₀-a.e. strongly measurable, and for H-a.e. x ∈ M₀ there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^N such that span τ is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M₀, θ₀) at x and ξ₀(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (M : ℕ → Set (Eucl N)) (θ : ℕ → Eucl N → ℝ) (ξ : ℕ → Eucl N → NVector (Eucl N) k) (M₀ : Set (Eucl N)) (θ₀ : Eucl N → ℝ) (ξ₀ : Eucl N → NVector (Eucl N) k), (∀ j, IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k (M j) (θ j) (ξ j)) → (∀ j, ∀ x ∈ M j, 1 ≤ θ j x) → NullMeasurableSet M₀ (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) → (∀ x ∈ M₀, 1 ≤ θ₀ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ₀ (M₀ ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)).restrict M₀), (∀ᶠ j in atTop, x ∈ M j) ∧ Tendsto (fun j => ξ j x) atTop (𝓝 (ξ₀ x))) → IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k M₀ θ₀ ξ₀

Source: Step 6 of the parent proof (the triple conditions for (M₊, θ, ξ) and the orientation argument), with the pointwise facts established there ("there is j(x) with θ_j(x) = θ(x) for j ≥ j(x); then x ∈ M_j … and ξ_j(x) → ξ(x)") isolated as hypotheses; it is the last paragraph of Simon's printed proof ("ξ_Q(x) ∈ Λ_n(T_xM_Q) … T_xM₊ = T_xM_Q except for a set of small measure … ξ(x) ∈ Λ_n(T_xM₊)"). It uses the siblings approx_tangent_locality (Lemma A) and weighted_tangent_equiv (Lemma B), the accepted sibling frame_sign (fiw_ims_frame_sign) and the library theorem HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique.

Notation. H := μHE[k]. For an H-null-measurable A, "H⌞A-a.e." means ∀ᵐ x ∂(H.restrict A). We use three facts about restricted measures: (R1) if A ⊆ B then H⌞A ≤ H⌞B, so an H⌞B-a.e. property holds H⌞A-a.e.; (R2) if A ⊆ B are H-null-measurable, a property holds H⌞A-a.e. iff "x ∈ A → property" holds H⌞B-a.e. (ae_restrict_iff'₀ and (H⌞B)⌞A = H⌞A); (R3) H⌞B-a.e. x lies in B (ae_restrict_mem₀). In particular, an H⌞M_j-a.e. property P yields, by (R1) for M_j ∩ M₀ ⊆ M_j, (R2) for M_j ∩ M₀ ⊆ M₀ and (R3), that "x ∈ M_j → P(x)" holds H⌞M₀-a.e.; we call this converting to H⌞M₀. W(A, ϑ, x, Q) abbreviates HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k A ϑ x Q and T(A, x, Q) abbreviates HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k A x Q. Let Good ⊆ M₀ be the set of x ∈ M₀ at which the hypothesis holds; H(M₀ ∖ Good) = 0.

1. (Local finiteness.) For every j and compact K, H(M_j ∩ K) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_j∩K} ENNReal.ofReal(θ_j) dH < ∞, because θ_j ≥ 1 on M_j and θ_j is H-integrable on M_j ∩ K (field integrableOn of the triple, K ⊆ univ). Likewise H(M₀ ∩ K) < ∞.

2. (Elementary fields.) subset: M₀ ⊆ univ. nullMeasurableSet: hypothesis. pos: θ₀ ≥ 1 > 0 on M₀. integrableOn: hypothesis, for every compact K ⊆ univ.

3. (Countable rectifiability.) Every x ∈ Good belongs to some M_j, so Z := M₀ ∖ ⋃_j M_j ⊆ M₀ ∖ Good is H-null. Z is countably k-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero), each M_j is (field countablyRectifiable of its triple), so the countable union Z ∪ ⋃_j M_j is countably k-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion applied to the sequence Z, M_0, M_1, …), and M₀ ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_j M_j is countably k-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).

4. (Measurability of ξ₀.) For each j, ξ_j is H⌞M_j-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable) and M_j is H-null-measurable, so g_j := M_j.indicator ξ_j is H-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀) and hence H⌞M₀-a.e. strongly measurable. For x ∈ Good, g_j(x) = ξ_j(x) for all large j, so g_j(x) → ξ₀(x). Thus ξ₀ is an H⌞M₀-a.e. limit of a.e. strongly measurable maps into NVector (Eucl N) k, a finite-dimensional normed space whose topology is metrizable, hence ξ₀ is H⌞M₀-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae).

5. (Tangent transfer.) Fix j. The following hold:
 (i) Lemma B (weighted_tangent_equiv) for E := M_j, θ := θ_j (null-measurable, locally finite by Step 1, θ_j > 0 and integrable on M_j ∩ K by the triple): H⌞M_j-a.e., ∀Q, W(M_j, θ_j, x, Q) ↔ T(M_j, x, Q).
 (ii) Lemma A (approx_tangent_locality) for E := M_j ∩ M₀ ⊆ E′ := M_j (both null-measurable, M_j locally finite): H⌞(M_j ∩ M₀)-a.e., ∀Q, T(M_j ∩ M₀, x, Q) ↔ T(M_j, x, Q).
 (iii) Lemma A for E := M_j ∩ M₀ ⊆ E′ := M₀ (M₀ locally finite): H⌞(M_j ∩ M₀)-a.e., ∀Q, T(M_j ∩ M₀, x, Q) ↔ T(M₀, x, Q).
 (iv) Lemma B for E := M₀, θ := θ₀ (θ₀ > 0, locally finite by Step 1, integrable by hypothesis): H⌞M₀-a.e., ∀Q, W(M₀, θ₀, x, Q) ↔ T(M₀, x, Q).
 Converting (i) to H⌞M₀, converting (ii) and (iii) to H⌞M₀ by (R2) for M_j ∩ M₀ ⊆ M₀ (with guard x ∈ M_j ∩ M₀, which by (R3) is x ∈ M_j for H⌞M₀-a.e. x), and chaining (i) →, (ii) ←, (iii) →, (iv) ←, we obtain (T_j): for H⌞M₀-a.e. x, if x ∈ M_j then for every Q, W(M_j, θ_j, x, Q) implies W(M₀, θ₀, x, Q).

6. (Orientation of the approximants.) For each j, the field orients of (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) holds H⌞M_j-a.e.; converting it to H⌞M₀ gives (O_j): for H⌞M₀-a.e. x, if x ∈ M_j then there is an orthonormal τ^j : Fin k → ℝ^N with W(M_j, θ_j, x, span τ^j) and ξ_j(x) = simpleNVector τ^j or ξ_j(x) = −simpleNVector τ^j.

7. (Orientation of the limit.) A countable intersection of H⌞M₀-a.e. properties holds H⌞M₀-a.e. (ae_all_iff), so for H⌞M₀-a.e. x: x ∈ Good, x ∈ M₀, and (T_j), (O_j) hold for every j. Fix such an x. Then θ₀(x) ≥ 1, so θ₀(x) ≠ 0; there is J with x ∈ M_j for all j ≥ J; and ξ_j(x) → ξ₀(x).
 - For j ≥ J, (O_j) gives an orthonormal τ^j with W(M_j, θ_j, x, span τ^j) and ξ_j(x) = ±simpleNVector τ^j, and (T_j) gives W(M₀, θ₀, x, span τ^j).
 - Uniqueness of the weighted approximate tangent space at a point where the weight is nonzero (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, θ₀(x) ≠ 0) gives span τ^J = span τ^j for every j ≥ J.
 - Put τ := τ^J and s := simpleNVector τ. For j ≥ J, frame_sign (fiw_ims_frame_sign with P := N, n := k, applied to the orthonormal families τ^J, τ^j with equal spans) gives simpleNVector τ^j = s or = −s; hence ξ_j(x) ∈ {s, −s} (using −(−s) = s).
 - The set {s, −s} is finite, hence closed in the Hausdorff space NVector (Eucl N) k. The sequence ξ_j(x) lies in it for all j ≥ J and converges to ξ₀(x), so ξ₀(x) ∈ {s, −s} (IsClosed.mem_of_tendsto).
 - Hence τ is orthonormal, W(M₀, θ₀, x, span τ) holds (case j = J of the first item), and ξ₀(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ₀(x) = −simpleNVector τ: the field orients of (M₀, θ₀, ξ₀) holds at x.

8. (Conclusion.) Steps 2, 3, 4 and 7 give all fields of IsRectifiableTriple univ k M₀ θ₀ ξ₀. ∎

It uses the siblings l1_cauchy_limit (imc_ae_tendsto_of_summable_lintegral), limit_triple (imc_isRectifiableTriple_of_eventually_mem), pairing_expansion (polyhedral_approx_pairing_expansion, comparator-accepted) and tau_integrable (ltg_tau_integrable, comparator-accepted).

Notation. H := μHE[k]. I := SimonMultiIndex k N (strictly increasing γ : Fin k → Fin N), m := #I. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For γ ∈ I: e_γ := (e_{γ(0)}, …, e_{γ(k−1)}), dx^γ := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (γ j)), and e^γ := simpleNVector e_γ ∈ Λ_k. For a k-covector α: α_γ := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α γ = α(e_γ) and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. ℝ^I := EuclideanSpace ℝ I with Euclidean norm ‖·‖. For a k-vector w: c(w) := (w(dx^γ))_γ ∈ ℝ^I, so ‖c(w)‖ = |w|. For a ∈ ℝ^I: L(a) := Σ_γ a_γ • e^γ ∈ Λ_k. κ_p := M_p.indicator(θ_p • ξ_p) and f_p := c ∘ κ_p : ℝ^N → ℝ^I.

0. Linear algebra.
 (a) c and L are ℝ-linear and continuous. Each coordinate of c is evaluation at the fixed covector dx^γ, and L is a finite sum of the continuous maps a ↦ a_γ • e^γ.
 (b) L(c(w)) = w for every k-vector w. For a covector α, L(c(w))(α) = Σ_γ w(dx^γ)·e^γ(α) = Σ_γ α(e_γ)·w(dx^γ) = Σ_γ α_γ·w(dx^γ) = w(α), by simpleNVector_apply and the first part of pairing_expansion. Two continuous linear functionals that agree everywhere are equal.
 (c) |L(a)(α)| ≤ m·‖a‖·|α| for a ∈ ℝ^I and every covector α. Indeed L(a)(α) = Σ_γ a_γ α_γ, with |a_γ| ≤ ‖a‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le) and |α_γ| ≤ |α| (second part of pairing_expansion).
 (d) (Unit fact.) If τ : Fin k → ℝ^N is orthonormal, then Σ_γ c_γ(simpleNVector τ)² = 1, hence ‖c(simpleNVector τ)‖ = ‖c(−simpleNVector τ)‖ = 1. Proof. Let α₀ := wedgeCovectors k (fun i ↦ innerSL ℝ (τ i)), the k-covector ⟨τ₁, ·⟩ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ⟨τ_k, ·⟩. By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, α₀(v) = det[⟨τ_i, v_j⟩]_{i,j}. Hence α₀(τ) = det[⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩] = det 1 = 1 by orthonormality, and α₀(e_γ) = det[⟨τ_i, e_{γ(j)}⟩] = det[(τ_i)_{γ(j)}]. On the other side, c_γ(simpleNVector τ) = dx^γ(τ) = det[proj_{γ(i)}(τ_j)] = det[(τ_j)_{γ(i)}], the determinant of the transpose; so α₀(e_γ) = c_γ(simpleNVector τ) (Matrix.det_transpose). The pairing expansion with w := simpleNVector τ and α := α₀ gives 1 = α₀(τ) = (simpleNVector τ)(α₀) = Σ_γ α₀(e_γ)·c_γ(simpleNVector τ) = Σ_γ c_γ(simpleNVector τ)². Finally c(−s) = −c(s) has the same norm as c(s).

1. (The coordinate sequence.)
 (a) θ_p ≥ 1 on M_p: θ_p(x) is a natural number (hypothesis) and is positive (field pos of the triple).
 (b) f_p is H-a.e. strongly measurable. Its γ-coordinate is x ↦ κ_p(x)(dx^γ) = M_p.indicator(x ↦ θ_p(x)·ξ_p(x)(dx^γ)). By tau_integrable (a) (U := univ, b := dx^γ, K := B̄_n(0)), the map x ↦ θ_p(x)ξ_p(x)(dx^γ) is H-integrable on M_p ∩ B̄_n(0) for every n ∈ ℕ. Hence it is H⌞M_p-a.e. strongly measurable, since M_p = ⋃_n (M_p ∩ B̄_n(0)) (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). As M_p is H-null-measurable, the indicator is H-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀). A map into the finite-dimensional space ℝ^I with a.e.-measurable coordinates is a.e. strongly measurable (aemeasurable_pi_iff, then compose with the continuous map WithLp.toLp).
 (c) ‖f_{p+1}(x) − f_p(x)‖ = ‖c(κ_{p+1}(x) − κ_p(x))‖ = |κ_{p+1}(x) − κ_p(x)|, by linearity of c and EuclideanSpace.norm_eq. Hence Σ_p ∫⁻ ‖f_{p+1} − f_p‖ₑ dH is the series of the hypothesis and is finite.
 (d) For H-a.e. x and every p, ‖f_p(x)‖ = M_p.indicator θ_p(x). If x ∉ M_p then κ_p(x) = 0 and both sides vanish. By the field orients of the triple (M_p, θ_p, ξ_p), for H⌞M_p-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ with ξ_p(x) = ±simpleNVector τ. For such x ∈ M_p, f_p(x) = θ_p(x)·c(ξ_p(x)) and ‖f_p(x)‖ = |θ_p(x)|·1 = θ_p(x), by 0(d) and θ_p(x) > 0. Convert the H⌞M_p-a.e. statement into an H-a.e. statement guarded by x ∈ M_p (ae_restrict_iff'₀), and intersect over the countably many p (ae_all_iff).

2. (L¹ limit.) By l1_cauchy_limit (X := ℝ^N, μ := H, E := ℝ^I, f := (f_p)_p; hypotheses 1(b) and 1(c)) there is an H-a.e. strongly measurable g : ℝ^N → ℝ^I with f_p(x) → g(x) for H-a.e. x and ∫⁻ ‖f_p − g‖ₑ dH → 0.

3. (Integer limit.) Let G be the set of x such that f_p(x) → g(x) and the identity of 1(d) holds for every p; then H(ℝ^N ∖ G) = 0. Fix x ∈ G and put a_p := ‖f_p(x)‖ = M_p.indicator θ_p(x). Each a_p is a natural number n_p (θ_p is natural on M_p and the indicator is 0 off M_p), and a_p → ‖g(x)‖. Choose P with |a_p − ‖g(x)‖| < 1/2 for all p ≥ P. Then |n_p − n_P| < 1, so n_p = n_P for every p ≥ P (Int.abs_lt_one_iff). Hence M_p.indicator θ_p(x) = n_P for all p ≥ P, and ‖g(x)‖ = lim a_p = n_P. Define θ₀(x) := ⌊‖g(x)‖ + 1/2⌋₊ for every x, a natural number. For x ∈ G, θ₀(x) = n_P = ‖g(x)‖ (as ⌊n + 1/2⌋₊ = n), and M_p.indicator θ_p(x) = θ₀(x) for all p ≥ P.

4. (The limit data.) Let M₀ := {x : θ₀(x) ≥ 1} and ξ₀(x) := θ₀(x)⁻¹ • L(g(x)).
 (a) θ₀ is natural-valued everywhere, in particular on M₀, and θ₀ ≥ 1 on M₀.
 (b) θ₀ is H-a.e. measurable: g is a.e. strongly measurable, the norm is continuous, and t ↦ (⌊t⌋₊ : ℝ) is monotone, hence Borel (Monotone.measurable). So M₀ = θ₀⁻¹([1, ∞)) is H-null-measurable.
 (c) θ₀ is H-integrable on M₀ ∩ K for every compact K. Choose p with ∫⁻ ‖f_p − g‖ₑ dH < ∞ (possible by Step 2). By 1(d), ∫⁻_K ‖f_p‖ₑ dH = ∫⁻_K M_p.indicator(‖θ_p‖ₑ) dH = ∫⁻_{M_p∩K} ‖θ_p‖ₑ dH < ∞, because θ_p is integrable on M_p ∩ K (field integrableOn of the triple). Since θ₀ = ‖g‖ H-a.e. (Step 3) and ‖g‖ ≤ ‖f_p‖ + ‖f_p − g‖, we get ∫⁻_{M₀∩K} ‖θ₀‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_K ‖g‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_K ‖f_p‖ₑ + ∫⁻ ‖f_p − g‖ₑ < ∞. Together with 4(b) this is integrability.
 (d) For H⌞M₀-a.e. x: x ∈ M_p for all large p, and ξ_p(x) → ξ₀(x). Indeed, H⌞M₀-a.e. x lies in M₀ (ae_restrict_mem₀) and in G. For such x, θ₀(x) = n ≥ 1, and M_p.indicator θ_p(x) = n ≠ 0 for p ≥ P; this forces x ∈ M_p and θ_p(x) = n = θ₀(x). For such p, κ_p(x) = θ₀(x) • ξ_p(x), so ξ_p(x) = θ₀(x)⁻¹ • κ_p(x) = θ₀(x)⁻¹ • L(c(κ_p(x))) = θ₀(x)⁻¹ • L(f_p(x)) by 0(b). This tends to θ₀(x)⁻¹ • L(g(x)) = ξ₀(x), because f_p(x) → g(x) and L is continuous.

5. (Rectifiable limit triple.) Apply limit_triple to (M_p, θ_p, ξ_p)_p and (M₀, θ₀, ξ₀). Its hypotheses hold: the triples by assumption, θ_p ≥ 1 on M_p (1(a)), M₀ null-measurable (4(b)), θ₀ ≥ 1 on M₀ (4(a)), local integrability (4(c)), and the pointwise convergence (4(d)). It gives IsRectifiableTriple ℝ^N k M₀ θ₀ ξ₀, and by 4(a) the multiplicity θ₀ is natural-valued on M₀.

6. (Convergence of the τ-actions.) Let ω : ℝ^N → Λ^k be continuous with compact support, and let C := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞. The map x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (covectorEuclideanNorm is the square root of a finite sum of squares of evaluations at fixed tuples, continuous_eval_const), and it has compact support since |0| = 0.
 (a) For every p, κ_p(x)(ω(x)) = M_p.indicator(θ_p·ξ_p(ω))(x). By tau_integrable (b) (U := univ) this is H-integrable, and tauAction k M_p θ_p ξ_p ω = ∫_{M_p} θ_pξ_p(ω) dH = ∫ κ_p(ω) dH (integral_indicator₀).
 (b) Likewise, with κ₀ := M₀.indicator(θ₀ • ξ₀), tau_integrable (b) for the triple of Step 5 shows that x ↦ κ₀(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable and tauAction k M₀ θ₀ ξ₀ ω = ∫ κ₀(ω) dH.
 (c) κ₀(x) = L(g(x)) for H-a.e. x (namely x ∈ G). If x ∈ M₀ then θ₀(x) ≠ 0 and κ₀(x) = θ₀(x) • θ₀(x)⁻¹ • L(g(x)) = L(g(x)). If x ∉ M₀ then θ₀(x) < 1 is a natural number, so θ₀(x) = 0 = ‖g(x)‖; hence g(x) = 0 and κ₀(x) = 0 = L(0).
 (d) For H-a.e. x, κ_p(x)(ω(x)) − κ₀(x)(ω(x)) = L(f_p(x))(ω(x)) − L(g(x))(ω(x)) = L(f_p(x) − g(x))(ω(x)), by 0(b), (c) and linearity of L. Its absolute value is ≤ m·C·‖f_p(x) − g(x)‖ by 0(c).
 (e) Hence ∫⁻ ‖κ_p(ω) − κ₀(ω)‖ₑ dH ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(mC)·∫⁻ ‖f_p − g‖ₑ dH → 0 by Step 2. The L¹ convergence theorem for Bochner integrals (tendsto_integral_of_L1, with 6(a) and 6(b)) then gives ∫ κ_p(ω) dH → ∫ κ₀(ω) dH, i.e. tauAction k M_p θ_p ξ_p ω → tauAction k M₀ θ₀ ξ₀ ω. ∎

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, in the localized form of Remark 3.7(2), on the whole space ℝ^Q. Simon proves 3.6 from the comparison theorem 3.3 and the 5-times covering lemma 3.4–3.5, and that printed argument is followed here. This is the fact invoked in Lemmas A and B of Step 5 of the parent proof: "H^k⌞(E′∖E) and ϑH^k⌞(E′∖E) have k-density 0 at H^k-a.e. x ∉ E′ ∖ E". Provenance: this child is the case W = ℝ^Q of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set (DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart-a1.zero_density_off_set-a1, candidate commit 12d217bba2a42bdf5072eede11b18f9349b61094), and this case is all that the siblings approx_tangent_locality and weighted_tangent_equiv use. Following the correction to this decomposition, it is a separate node under the fresh name imc_ae_zero_density_off_set. Its frozen type differs from that of every existing DAG node, and there is no cross-branch dependency. The Lean proof reproduced at the end embeds the accepted proof, for an arbitrary open W, as a local `have` and specializes it to W = univ. It compiles.

Notation. μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q. By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, μ = c_n·μH[n] for a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞), where μH[n] is Mathlib's unnormalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure (covers by sets of small diameter, cost Σ diamⁿ). B̄_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ and B_ρ(y) := ball y ρ. Powers of radii are taken in [0, ∞] as ofReal(ρ)ⁿ = ofReal(ρⁿ) (ρ ≥ 0).

1. (The weighted measure.) Let ν := (μ⌞S).withDensity g, a Borel measure on ℝ^Q (no measurability of S or g is needed to form it). For every Borel B, ν(B) = ∫⁻_B g d(μ⌞S) = ∫⁻_{S∩B} g dμ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). In particular ν(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dμ, and ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K.

2. (Borel hull.) Let A := toMeasurable μ S. A is Borel, S ⊆ A, and A = S μ-a.e. because S is μ-null-measurable. Moreover ν(Aᶜ) = ∫⁻_{S∩Aᶜ} g dμ = 0, since S ∩ Aᶜ = ∅.

3. (Core estimate; Simon 3.3 and 3.6.) Let m be a finite Borel measure on ℝ^Q with m(Aᶜ) = 0, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞). Put Z_ε := {y ∉ A : for every δ > 0 there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with ε·ρⁿ < m(B̄_ρ(y))}. Claim: μH[n](Z_ε) = 0.
 (a) Fix k ∈ ℕ. A finite Borel measure on a metric space is inner regular on Borel sets with respect to closed sets, so there is a closed C ⊆ A with m(A ∖ C) < 1/k (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt).
 (b) Let 𝓣 be the family of pairs (y, ρ) with y ∈ Z_ε, 0 < ρ < 1/(k+1), B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ ℝ^Q ∖ C and ε·ρⁿ < m(B̄_ρ(y)). Each y ∈ Z_ε lies in the open set ℝ^Q ∖ C, because y ∉ A ⊇ C. Choose δ₀ > 0 with B_{δ₀}(y) ⊆ ℝ^Q ∖ C, and apply the definition of Z_ε with min{δ, δ₀, 1/(k+1)}. So for every δ > 0 there is (y, ρ) ∈ 𝓣 with ρ < δ: the closed balls of 𝓣 cover Z_ε finely.
 (c) By the Vitali 5r-covering lemma (Simon 3.4–3.5; Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily 𝓤 ⊆ 𝓣 such that every ball of 𝓣, in particular a small ball centred at any given y ∈ Z_ε, is contained in B̄_{5ρ′}(y′) for some (y′, ρ′) ∈ 𝓤. Hence Z_ε ⊆ ⋃_{(y,ρ)∈𝓤} B̄_{5ρ}(y). The family 𝓤 is countable: its balls are pairwise disjoint with nonempty interior in the separable space ℝ^Q.
 (d) ε·Σ_{(y,ρ)∈𝓤} ρⁿ ≤ Σ_{(y,ρ)∈𝓤} m(B̄_ρ(y)) = m(⋃_{(y,ρ)∈𝓤} B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ m(ℝ^Q ∖ C) ≤ m(A ∖ C) + m(Aᶜ) < 1/k. This uses disjointness of the balls, B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ ℝ^Q ∖ C, and m(Aᶜ) = 0.
 (e) The balls B̄_{5ρ}(y), (y, ρ) ∈ 𝓤, cover Z_ε and have diameter ≤ 10ρ < 10/(k+1). Also Σ diam(B̄_{5ρ}(y))ⁿ ≤ 10ⁿ Σ ρⁿ ≤ 10ⁿ/(kε). These covers have mesh → 0 as k → ∞, so μH[n](Z_ε) ≤ liminf_k 10ⁿ/(kε) = 0 (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum).

4. (Localization; Simon Remark 3.7(2).) Let E := {y ∉ A : ν(B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) does not tend to 0 as ρ → 0+}. We show μ(E) = 0. ℝ^Q is second countable, so by measure_null_of_locally_null it suffices that every y₀ ∈ E has a neighbourhood U with μ(E ∩ U) = 0. Let y₀ ∈ E and put m := ν⌞B̄_{2/3}(y₀). It is finite, because B̄_{2/3}(y₀) is compact (Step 1), and m(Aᶜ) ≤ ν(Aᶜ) = 0. Let U := B_{1/3}(y₀) and y ∈ E ∩ U. Since the quotient does not tend to 0, there is ε₀ > 0 with ν(B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) > ε₀ for arbitrarily small ρ > 0. Pick j ∈ ℕ with 1/(j+1) < ε₀. For ρ < 1/3, B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B̄_{2/3}(y₀), so m(B̄_ρ(y)) = ν(B̄_ρ(y)) > (1/(j+1))·ρⁿ for such arbitrarily small ρ. Hence y ∈ Z_{1/(j+1)} for this m, and E ∩ U ⊆ ⋃_j Z_{1/(j+1)}. This union is μH[n]-null by Step 3, hence μ-null (μ = c_n·μH[n]). (The Lean proof below does the same with an arbitrary open W ⊇ B̄_{2R/3}(y₀) and specializes it to W = ℝ^Q.)

5. (Back from A to S.) For μ-a.e. y, y ∈ A ⇔ y ∈ S (A = S μ-a.e.). Hence for μ-a.e. y: if y ∉ S, then y ∉ A and y ∉ E (Step 4), so ν(B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) → 0. By Step 1 this quotient equals (∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dμ)/ofReal(ρⁿ). ∎ For n = 0 the same argument applies verbatim.


Formalization note. The Lean proof below embeds, as the local `have hgen`, the comparator-accepted proof of Submission.lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set (candidate commit 12d217bb) for an arbitrary open W, unchanged except for indentation, and then specializes it to W = univ. It compiles against the frozen commit d8d46c9 (default maxHeartbeats, no set_option, no sorry; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Inside hgen: hνB is Step 1, hνA is Step 2, hcore is Step 3 (Vitali covering), hmain is Step 4, and the final filter_upwards is Step 5.

```lean
theorem Submission.imc_ae_zero_density_off_set :
    ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (S : Set (Eucl Q)) (g : Eucl Q → ℝ≥0∞), NullMeasurableSet S (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → ∫⁻ x in S ∩ K, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) < ∞) → ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)), y ∉ S → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (∫⁻ x in S ∩ closedBall y ρ, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) / ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) := by
  intro Q n S g hS hfinS
  -- the localized statement for an arbitrary open `W` (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2))
  have hgen :
      ∀ W : Set (Eucl Q), IsOpen W → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → ∫⁻ x in S ∩ K, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) < ∞) → ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)), y ∈ W → y ∉ S → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (∫⁻ x in S ∩ closedBall y ρ, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) / ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) := by
    intro W hW hfin
    set μ : Measure (Eucl Q) := μHE[n] with hμ
    -- Step 1: `ν = (μ ⌞ S).withDensity g`, so `ν B = ∫⁻_{S ∩ B} g dμ` for Borel `B`.
    set ν : Measure (Eucl Q) := (μ.restrict S).withDensity g with hν
    have hνB : ∀ B : Set (Eucl Q), MeasurableSet B → ν B = ∫⁻ x in S ∩ B, g x ∂μ := by
      intro B hB
      rw [hν, withDensity_apply _ hB, Measure.restrict_restrict hB, inter_comm B S]
    -- Step 2: the Borel hull `A ⊇ S` of `S`; `ν` does not charge `Aᶜ`.
    set A : Set (Eucl Q) := toMeasurable μ S
    have hAm : MeasurableSet A := measurableSet_toMeasurable μ S
    have hνA : ν Aᶜ = 0 := by
      rw [hνB _ hAm.compl,
        (disjoint_compl_right_iff_subset.mpr (subset_toMeasurable μ S)).inter_eq,
        Measure.restrict_empty, lintegral_zero_measure]
    -- `diam B̄_s(c) ≤ 2s`.
    have hdiam : ∀ (c : Eucl Q) (s : ℝ), ediam (closedBall c s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * s) :=
      fun c s => ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le fun y hy z hz => by
        have := dist_triangle_right y z c
        rw [mem_closedBall] at hy hz
        linarith
    -- Step 4 (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6): for a finite `m` with `m Aᶜ = 0`, the
    -- points `y ∉ A` of upper density `> ε` form an `Hⁿ`-null set.  Proof: a closed `C ⊆ A`
    -- with `m (A \ C) < k⁻¹`, then a Vitali 5r-covering by disjoint balls of radius `< 1/(k+1)`
    -- missing `C`, whose total `ρⁿ`-cost is at most `k⁻¹ / ε`.
    have hcore : ∀ m : Measure (Eucl Q), m univ ≠ ∞ → m Aᶜ = 0 → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, ε ≠ 0 → ε ≠ ∞ →
        μH[n] {y | y ∉ A ∧ ∀ δ > 0, ∃ ρ ∈ Ioo 0 δ,
          ε * ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n < m (closedBall y ρ)} = 0 := by
      intro m hm hmA ε hε0 hεtop
      set Z := {y | y ∉ A ∧ ∀ δ > 0, ∃ ρ ∈ Ioo 0 δ,
        ε * ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n < m (closedBall y ρ)}
      have : IsFiniteMeasure m := ⟨lt_top_iff_ne_top.mpr hm⟩
      have hstep : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ u : Set (Eucl Q × ℝ), u.Countable ∧
          (∀ b ∈ u, b.2 ∈ Ioo 0 (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1))) ∧
          Z ⊆ ⋃ b ∈ u, closedBall b.1 (5 * b.2) ∧
          ε * ∑' b : u, ENNReal.ofReal b.1.2 ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := by
        intro k
        obtain ⟨C, hCA, hCc, hCm⟩ := hAm.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt (μ := m) (measure_ne_top m A)
          (ENNReal.inv_ne_zero.mpr (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top k))
        let t : Set (Eucl Q × ℝ) := {b | b.1 ∈ Z ∧ b.2 ∈ Ioo 0 (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
          closedBall b.1 b.2 ⊆ Cᶜ ∧ ε * ENNReal.ofReal b.2 ^ n < m (closedBall b.1 b.2)}
        obtain ⟨u, hut, hudisj, hucov⟩ :=
          Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall t Prod.fst Prod.snd
            (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) (fun b hb => hb.2.1.2.le) 5 (by norm_num)
        have hucount : u.Countable := hudisj.countable_of_nonempty_interior fun b hb =>
          (nonempty_ball.mpr (hut hb).2.1.1).mono ball_subset_interior_closedBall
        refine ⟨u, hucount, fun b hb => (hut hb).2.1, ?_, ?_⟩
        · -- each `y ∈ Z` lies outside the closed `C ⊆ A`, so it centers small good balls `⊆ Cᶜ`
          intro y hy
          obtain ⟨δ₀, hδ₀, hδ₀C⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.mp hCc.isOpen_compl y fun h => hy.1 (hCA h)
          obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, hρm⟩ := hy.2 (min δ₀ (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1))) (by positivity)
          have hρC : closedBall y ρ ⊆ Cᶜ :=
            (closedBall_subset_ball (hρ.2.trans_le (min_le_left _ _))).trans hδ₀C
          obtain ⟨b, hbu, hb⟩ :=
            hucov (y, ρ) ⟨hy, ⟨hρ.1, hρ.2.trans_le (min_le_right _ _)⟩, hρC, hρm⟩
          exact mem_iUnion₂.mpr ⟨b, hbu, hb (mem_closedBall_self hρ.1.le)⟩
        · have := hucount.to_subtype
          calc ε * ∑' b : u, ENNReal.ofReal b.1.2 ^ n
              = ∑' b : u, ε * ENNReal.ofReal b.1.2 ^ n := ENNReal.tsum_mul_left.symm
            _ ≤ ∑' b : u, m (closedBall b.1.1 b.1.2 ∩ Cᶜ) := ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun b => by
                rw [inter_eq_left.mpr (hut b.2).2.2.1]
                exact (hut b.2).2.2.2.le
            _ = m (⋃ b : u, closedBall b.1.1 b.1.2 ∩ Cᶜ) := (measure_iUnion
                (fun i j hij => (hudisj i.2 j.2 (Subtype.coe_ne_coe.mpr hij)).mono
                  inter_subset_left inter_subset_left)
                (fun _ => measurableSet_closedBall.inter hCc.isOpen_compl.measurableSet)).symm
            _ ≤ m Cᶜ := measure_mono (iUnion_subset fun _ => inter_subset_right)
            _ ≤ m ((A \ C) ∪ Aᶜ) := measure_mono fun x hx => by
                by_cases h : x ∈ A
                exacts [Or.inl ⟨h, hx⟩, Or.inr h]
            _ ≤ m (A \ C) + m Aᶜ := measure_union_le _ _
            _ ≤ (k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := by
                rw [hmA, add_zero]
                exact hCm.le
      choose u hucount hurad hucov husum using hstep
      have : ∀ k, Countable (u k) := fun k => (hucount k).to_subtype
      refine le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
      calc μH[n] Z ≤ liminf (fun k => ∑' b : u k, ediam (closedBall b.1.1 (5 * b.1.2)) ^ (n : ℝ))
            atTop := by
            refine Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum (n : ℝ) Z
              (fun k : ℕ => ENNReal.ofReal (10 * (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)))) ?_
              (fun k (b : u k) => closedBall b.1.1 (5 * b.1.2)) ?_ ?_
            · simpa using ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal
                ((tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜 := ℝ)).const_mul 10)
            · refine Eventually.of_forall fun k b => (hdiam _ _).trans (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal ?_)
              have := (hurad k b.1 b.2).2
              linarith
            · refine Eventually.of_forall fun k y hy => ?_
              obtain ⟨b, hbu, hb⟩ := mem_iUnion₂.mp (hucov k hy)
              exact mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨⟨b, hbu⟩, hb⟩
        _ ≤ liminf (fun k : ℕ => 10 ^ n * ((k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ / ε)) atTop := by
            refine liminf_le_liminf (Eventually.of_forall fun k => ?_)
            calc ∑' b : u k, ediam (closedBall b.1.1 (5 * b.1.2)) ^ (n : ℝ)
                ≤ ∑' b : u k, 10 ^ n * ENNReal.ofReal b.1.2 ^ n :=
                  ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun b => by
                    rw [ENNReal.rpow_natCast, ← mul_pow]
                    gcongr
                    refine (hdiam _ _).trans ?_
                    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat 10, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by norm_num)]
                    exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (by linarith)
              _ = 10 ^ n * ∑' b : u k, ENNReal.ofReal b.1.2 ^ n := ENNReal.tsum_mul_left
              _ ≤ 10 ^ n * ((k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ / ε) := by
                  gcongr
                  rw [ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le (Or.inl hε0) (Or.inl hεtop), mul_comm]
                  exact husum k
        _ = 0 := by
            refine Tendsto.liminf_eq ?_
            simpa using ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul
              (ENNReal.Tendsto.div_const ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero (Or.inr hε0))
              (Or.inr (ENNReal.pow_ne_top ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top))
    -- Steps 3 and 5: localize to balls `B̄_{2r}(x) ⊆ W` (finite `ν`-mass) around each point of
    -- the exceptional set, and use `μHE[n] = c • μH[n]`.
    have hmain : ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, y ∈ W → y ∉ A →
        Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (closedBall y ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) := by
      rw [ae_iff]
      apply measure_null_of_locally_null
      intro x hx
      simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, not_imp] at hx
      obtain ⟨R, hR, hRW⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.mp hW x hx.1
      have hr : 0 < R / 3 := by positivity
      have hKW : closedBall x (2 * (R / 3)) ⊆ W := (closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith)).trans hRW
      set m := ν.restrict (closedBall x (2 * (R / 3))) with hm_def
      have hm : m univ ≠ ∞ := by
        rw [hm_def, Measure.restrict_apply_univ, hνB _ measurableSet_closedBall]
        exact (hfin _ (isCompact_closedBall x _) hKW).ne
      have hmA : m Aᶜ = 0 := by
        rw [hm_def, Measure.restrict_apply hAm.compl]
        exact measure_mono_null inter_subset_left hνA
      refine ⟨_ ∩ ball x (R / 3), inter_mem_nhdsWithin _ (ball_mem_nhds x hr), ?_⟩
      rw [hμ, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, Measure.smul_apply]
      refine (congrArg _ (measure_mono_null ?_ (measure_iUnion_null fun k : ℕ =>
        hcore m hm hmA ((k : ℝ≥0∞) + 1)⁻¹ (by simp) (by simp)))).trans (smul_zero _)
      -- a non-tending quotient exceeds some `(k + 1)⁻¹` at arbitrarily small radii
      rintro y ⟨hy, hyx⟩
      simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, not_imp] at hy
      obtain ⟨-, hyA, hyT⟩ := hy
      rw [ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero] at hyT
      push Not at hyT
      obtain ⟨ε, hε, hfreq⟩ := hyT
      obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt hε.ne'
      refine mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨k, hyA, fun δ hδ => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨ρ, hρf, hρ⟩ := (hfreq.and_eventually (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT (lt_min hδ hr))).exists
      refine ⟨ρ, ⟨hρ.1, hρ.2.trans_le (min_le_left _ _)⟩, ?_⟩
      have hsub : closedBall y ρ ⊆ closedBall x (2 * (R / 3)) := by
        intro z hz
        rw [mem_closedBall] at hz ⊢
        rw [mem_ball] at hyx
        linarith [dist_triangle z y x, hρ.2.trans_le (min_le_right δ (R / 3))]
      rw [hm_def, Measure.restrict_apply measurableSet_closedBall, inter_eq_left.mpr hsub,
        ← ENNReal.ofReal_pow hρ.1.le]
      refine ENNReal.mul_lt_of_lt_div (lt_of_le_of_lt ?_ hρf)
      exact (ENNReal.inv_le_inv.mpr (by simp)).trans hk.le
    -- Step 6: transfer from the hull `A` back to `S` (they agree `μ`-a.e.).
    filter_upwards [hmain, hS.toMeasurable_ae_eq] with y hy hyA hyW hyS
    refine (hy hyW fun h => hyS (hyA ▸ h)).congr fun ρ => ?_
    rw [hνB _ measurableSet_closedBall]
  filter_upwards [hgen univ isOpen_univ fun K hK _ => hfinS K hK] with y hy hyS
  exact hy (mem_univ y) hyS
```

proof_key_steps: ν := (Hⁿ⌞S).withDensity g has ν(B) = ∫⁻_{S∩B} g dHⁿ for Borel B, is finite on compact sets, and ν(Aᶜ) = 0 for the Borel hull A = toMeasurable Hⁿ S.

Simon 3.3/3.6: for a finite m with m(Aᶜ) = 0, the set of y ∉ A with m(B̄_ρ(y)) > ερⁿ for arbitrarily small ρ is μH[n]-null: closed C ⊆ A with m(A∖C) < 1/k, Vitali 5r-cover by disjoint balls inside Cᶜ, cost ≤ 10ⁿ/(kε).
Localize ν to compact balls B̄_{2/3}(y₀) (measure_null_of_locally_null): a non-vanishing quotient at y ∈ B_{1/3}(y₀) places y in some Z_{1/(j+1)}.
Pass from the hull A back to S (A = S a.e.) and rewrite ν(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of the n-vector/n-covector pairing (Simon 1.5–1.7)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-vector w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (a continuous linear functional on n-covectors, `NVector`) and every n-covector c ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) (a continuous alternating map, `Covector`): w(c) = Σ_I c_I · w(dx^I), where I ranges over the strictly increasing multi-indices Fin n ↪o Fin P (`SimonMultiIndex n P`), c_I := c(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)}) (`euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I`) and dx^I := dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n−1)} (`wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))`). Moreover |c_I| ≤ |c| for every I, where |c| is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm (`covectorEuclideanNorm c`).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 be the standard basis; EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k = e_k (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). An n-covector is a continuous alternating map c : Eⁿ → ℝ (Covector E n). An n-vector w is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (NVector E n). For J : Fin n → Fin P write e_J := (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}). For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, i.e. an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P (a strictly increasing map), put c_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I = c(e_I) and dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)).

1. (dx^I on increasing basis tuples.) By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for every J : Fin n → Fin P, dx^I(e_J) = det(Matrix.of fun i j => proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)})) = det[δ_{I(i),J(j)}]_{i,j}.
   - If J = ⇑I, the matrix is the identity, so dx^I(e_I) = 1.
   - If J = ⇑I′ for some I′ ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with I′ ≠ I, then range I ≠ range I′. Indeed, a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the unique order embedding onto its range, so it is determined by its range. Both ranges have exactly n elements, so some I(i) ∉ range I′. Row i of the matrix is then zero, and dx^I(e_{I′}) = 0.
   Hence dx^I(e_{I′}) = 1 if I′ = I and 0 otherwise.
2. (Sorting injective tuples.) Let J : Fin n → Fin P be injective and s := range J, a Finset of card n. Let I_J := s.orderEmbOfFin (card s = n) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P be the increasing enumeration of s (Finset.orderEmbOfFin); then range I_J = s. Since I_J is a bijection Fin n → s and J takes values in s, σ := I_J⁻¹ ∘ J is a permutation of Fin n with J = I_J ∘ σ. For every alternating map α on Eⁿ, AlternatingMap.map_perm gives α(e_J) = α(e_{I_J} ∘ σ) = sign(σ)·α(e_{I_J}).
3. (c = Σ_I c_I dx^I.) Let c′ := Σ_I c_I·dx^I ∈ Covector E n.
   - For I′ ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, step 1 gives c′(e_{I′}) = Σ_I c_I·[I = I′] = c_{I′} = c(e_{I′}).
   - For injective J, step 2 applied to c′ and to c gives c′(e_J) = sign(σ)·c′(e_{I_J}) = sign(σ)·c(e_{I_J}) = c(e_J).
   - By Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the underlying alternating maps and the standard basis of E, two alternating maps that agree on all tuples of pairwise distinct basis vectors are equal. Hence c′ = c as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ext).
   - Degenerate cases are included. For n > P there is no injective J and no I, and both c and c′ are 0. For n = 0 there is exactly one I (the empty embedding), dx^∅ is the constant covector 1, and c = c(∅)·1.
4. (Pairing.) w is linear, so w(c) = w(Σ_I c_I·dx^I) = Σ_I c_I·w(dx^I) (map_sum, map_smul). This is the first conjunct.
5. (Coordinate bound.) By definition covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S, where S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} (if StrictMono J then c(fun i => basisFun (J i))² else 0) is a sum of nonnegative terms. For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, ⇑I is StrictMono and basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i) = e_{I(i)}, so the summand for J = ⇑I equals c_I². Hence c_I² ≤ S (Finset.single_le_sum), and |c_I| = √(c_I²) ≤ √S = covectorEuclideanNorm c (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). This is the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^I(e_{I′}) = δ_{I,I′} for increasing I, I′, from the determinant formula wedgeCovectors_apply_det.
Every injective basis tuple is a permutation of an increasing one: α(e_J) = sign σ · α(e_{I_J}).
Module.Basis.ext_alternating gives c = Σ_I c_I dx^I.
Linearity of w gives w(c) = Σ_I c_I w(dx^I).
c_I² is one nonnegative summand of covectorEuclideanNorm(c)², so |c_I| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm c.

subproblems.statement:
Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (k-vectors, `NVector`) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ. Write H := Hᵏ = μHE[k].
(a) For every compact K ⊆ U and every k-covector b, the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
(b) For every continuous k-covector field ω : ℝ^P → Λᵏ(ℝ^P) with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U, the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M.

Source: facts (F0), (F2) and the remark 'All integrands are integrable' in step 7 of the parent proof, written out.

Notation. H := μHE[k]. For a k-covector α (a continuous alternating k-linear map), ‖α‖ is its operator norm, so |α(v₁,…,v_k)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |v_j|. The fields of IsRectifiableTriple used are nullMeasurableSet, integrableOn, aestronglyMeasurable and orients.

1. (Unit bound, F0.) For H⌞M-a.e. x and every k-covector α: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
 By `orients`, for H⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. Since simpleNVector τ (α) = α(τ₁,…,τ_k), we get |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |τ_j| = ‖α‖, because |τ_j| = 1. For k = 0 the empty product is 1.

2. (Measurability.) Let ω : ℝ^P → Λᵏ be continuous. The evaluation map Λ_k × Λᵏ → ℝ, (w, α) ↦ w(α), is continuous. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M (`aestronglyMeasurable`), and ω is continuous. Hence x ↦ (ξ(x), ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M, and so is its composition x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) with the evaluation map. The same holds for H⌞S whenever S ⊆ M, since H⌞S ≤ H⌞M. Taking ω constant equal to b gives the same for x ↦ ξ(x)(b).

3. (Part (a).) Let K ⊆ U be compact and b a k-covector.
 - By `integrableOn`, θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
 - Since M ∩ K ⊆ M, step 1 gives |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x.
 - By step 2, x ↦ ξ(x)(b) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K).
 The product of an integrable function with an a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded function is integrable. So x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.

4. (Part (b) on the support.) Let ω be continuous with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. Put K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U.
 - Being continuous with compact support, ω is bounded: |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x, for some C.
 - θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (`integrableOn`).
 - x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K) (step 2), and |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x (step 1).
 As in step 3, h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.

5. (Part (b), conclusion.) If x ∈ M \ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and h(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0. M is H-null-measurable (`nullMeasurableSet`) and M ∩ K ⊆ M. A function integrable on M ∩ K that vanishes on M \ (M ∩ K) is integrable on the null-measurable set M. Hence h is H-integrable on M. ∎

- Step 2: `Continuous.clm_apply continuous_fst continuous_snd`, composed via `Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable` with `hT.aestronglyMeasurable.prodMk hω.aestronglyMeasurable`. Note: `continuous_eval` fails, because the instance `ContinuousEval (NVector (Eucl P) k) (Covector (Eucl P) k) ℝ` is not found.
- Steps 3–4: `Integrable.bdd_mul`, together with `ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset inter_subset_left` and `AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure (Measure.restrict_mono inter_subset_left le_rfl)`. The bound C comes from `Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`.
- Step 5: `IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero hT.nullMeasurableSet` and `image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport`.
- Do not use Integrable/IntegrableOn of NVector-valued functions: `ContinuousENorm (NVector (Eucl P) k)` does not synthesize.
proof_key_steps: Orientation (ξ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_k with τ orthonormal) gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for H⌞M-a.e. x and every covector α.
x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable: continuous evaluation composed with (ξ, ω).
An integrable function (θ on M ∩ K) times an a.e.-bounded measurable factor is integrable. This gives (a), and gives (b) on M ∩ tsupport ω.
The integrand of (b) vanishes on M \ tsupport ω, so it is integrable on the null-measurable set M.

subproblems.title: Lusin decomposition of (M, θ) into compact pieces with continuous weight (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let V ⊆ ℝ^Q be open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V. Then there are sets C_k ⊆ ℝ^Q (k ∈ ℕ) such that each C_k is compact, C_k ⊆ M, θ|C_k is continuous, Hⁿ(C_k) < ∞, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1): "by Lusin's Theorem 1.17 of Ch. 1, there is an increasing sequence {M_j} of compact subsets of M with Hⁿ(M ∖ ∪M_j) = 0 and θ|M_j continuous (hence has a positive lower bound, hence Hⁿ(M_j) < ∞)"). Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q.

1. (Countable compact cover of V.) Let D ⊆ ℝ^Q be a countable dense set (`TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense`). Let 𝒦 be the countable family of closed balls B̄_t(q) with q ∈ D, t ∈ ℚ, t > 0 and B̄_t(q) ⊆ V. Each member is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^Q) and contained in V. Every x ∈ V lies in some member: V is open, so there is a rational t > 0 with B̄_{2t}(x) ⊆ V; pick q ∈ D with |q − x| < t; then x ∈ B̄_t(q) ⊆ B̄_{2t}(x) ⊆ V. If 𝒦 = ∅ then V = ∅ = M and C_k := ∅ works; otherwise enumerate 𝒦 = {K_i : i ∈ ℕ}. Then V = ⋃_i K_i, so M = ⋃_i M_i with M_i := M ∩ K_i.

2. (A Borel core of M_i on which θ is Borel.) Fix i. By hypothesis θ is μ-integrable on M_i; in particular θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞M_i, so there are a Borel function θ̃_i : ℝ^Q → ℝ and a Borel set Z_i with μ(Z_i ∩ M_i) = 0 such that θ = θ̃_i on M_i ∖ Z_i. Since M and K_i are μ-null-measurable, so is M_i, hence there is a Borel set B_i⁰ ⊆ M_i with μ(M_i ∖ B_i⁰) = 0 (`NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`). Put B_i := B_i⁰ ∖ Z_i: B_i is Borel, B_i ⊆ M_i, μ(M_i ∖ B_i) ≤ μ(M_i ∖ B_i⁰) + μ(M_i ∩ Z_i) = 0, and θ = θ̃_i on B_i.

3. (A finite Borel measure.) Let ν_i := (μ⌞B_i).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ̃_i), so ν_i(E) = ∫⁻_{B_i ∩ E} ofReal(θ̃_i) dμ for Borel E (`withDensity_apply`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`). Then ν_i(ℝ^Q) = ∫⁻_{B_i} ofReal(θ) dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞. A finite Borel measure on a metric space is weakly regular (`Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure`), so for every Borel E with ν_i(E) < ∞ and every δ > 0 there is a closed F ⊆ E with ν_i(E ∖ F) < δ (`MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt`).

4. (Lusin.) Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable`, Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter01/Lusin.lean), applied to ν_i with the regularity of step 3, the Borel set B_i (ν_i(B_i) < ∞), the Borel function θ̃_i and ε := 1/(j + 1) (j ∈ ℕ), yields closed sets F_{i,j} ⊆ B_i with ν_i(B_i ∖ F_{i,j}) < 1/(j + 1) and θ̃_i|F_{i,j} continuous. As θ = θ̃_i on B_i ⊇ F_{i,j}, θ|F_{i,j} is continuous (`ContinuousOn.congr`). F_{i,j} is closed and contained in the compact set K_i, hence compact; and F_{i,j} ⊆ B_i ⊆ M.

5. (Finite measure of the pieces.) If F_{i,j} ≠ ∅, the continuous function θ attains its minimum m on the compact set F_{i,j} (`IsCompact.exists_isMinOn`), and m > 0 because F_{i,j} ⊆ M. Then m · μ(F_{i,j}) ≤ ∫⁻_{F_{i,j}} ofReal(θ) dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞, so μ(F_{i,j}) < ∞. If F_{i,j} = ∅, μ(F_{i,j}) = 0.

6. (Null remainder.) G_i := B_i ∖ ⋃_j F_{i,j} is Borel and ν_i(G_i) ≤ ν_i(B_i ∖ F_{i,j}) < 1/(j + 1) for every j, so ν_i(G_i) = ∫⁻_{G_i} ofReal(θ̃_i) dμ = 0. The integrand ofReal ∘ θ̃_i is measurable, and on G_i ⊆ B_i ⊆ M it equals ofReal(θ) > 0; by `lintegral_eq_zero_iff` it vanishes μ⌞G_i-a.e., which forces μ(G_i) = 0. Therefore μ(M_i ∖ ⋃_j F_{i,j}) ≤ μ(M_i ∖ B_i) + μ(G_i) = 0.

7. (Enumeration.) Let (C_k)_{k∈ℕ} enumerate the countable family (F_{i,j})_{i,j∈ℕ}, e.g. C_k := F_{(Nat.unpair k).1,(Nat.unpair k).2}. Each C_k is compact, C_k ⊆ M, θ|C_k is continuous (ContinuousOn θ C_k) and μ(C_k) < ∞ (steps 4, 5). Since M = ⋃_i M_i, M ∖ ⋃_k C_k ⊆ ⋃_i (M_i ∖ ⋃_j F_{i,j}), a countable union of μ-null sets (step 6); hence μ(M ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. ∎

B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is item 0(d) of the parent proof (η_{y,r} is a similarity of ratio r⁻¹), proved for every g.

1. (η is a measurable equivalence.) Since r ≠ 0, η(x) = r⁻¹(x − y) has the inverse ψ(z) = y + r z. Both maps are continuous affine maps of ℝ^Q, so η is a homeomorphism and hence a measurable equivalence e : ℝ^Q ≃ᵐ ℝ^Q (Borel σ-algebra) with e = η and e⁻¹ = ψ. In particular η is a measurable embedding and η⁻¹(η(S)) = S for every set S.

2. (Push-forward of Hⁿ.) Put μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q. Claim: μ.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ. Let B be a Borel set. Then (μ.map η)(B) = μ(η⁻¹(B)) = μ(ψ(B)), and ψ(B) = τ_y(r • B) where τ_y(z) = y + z. The translation τ_y is an isometry of ℝ^Q, so μ(τ_y(r • B)) = μ(r • B) (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`). Since r ≠ 0, μ(r • B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ • μ(B) (`MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`). As r > 0, ‖r‖₊ⁿ = rⁿ and its image in [0, ∞] is ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ). Thus (μ.map η)(B) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) · μ(B) for every Borel B, and two measures agreeing on all Borel sets are equal. (Equivalently one may use `MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`, since ψ is a homothety of ratio r composed with a translation.)

3. (Restriction.) For a measurable equivalence e and any set s (measurable or not), (μ.map e).restrict s = (μ.restrict (e⁻¹(s))).map e (`MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map`). Taking s := η(S) and using e⁻¹(η(S)) = S (step 1) and step 2:
 (μ.restrict S).map η = (μ.map η).restrict (η(S)) = (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ).restrict (η(S)) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • (μ.restrict (η(S))) (`Measure.restrict_smul`).

4. (Integrals.) For a measurable embedding η and any measure ν, ∫ g d(ν.map η) = ∫ g(η(x)) dν(x) for every function g, integrable or not (`MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map`). With ν := μ.restrict S and step 3:
 ∫_S g(η(x)) dμ(x) = ∫ g d((μ.restrict S).map η) = ∫ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ.restrict(η(S))) = (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)).toReal · ∫_{η(S)} g dμ = rⁿ ∫_{η(S)} g dμ,
 using `integral_smul_measure` (valid for every g) and (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)).toReal = rⁿ because rⁿ ≥ 0.

5. (Conclusion.) Since rⁿ > 0, multiplying by (rⁿ)⁻¹ gives ∫_{η(S)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η(x)) dHⁿ(x). ∎ (For n = 0 this reads ∫_{η(S)} g dH⁰ = ∫_S g∘η dH⁰, consistent with H⁰ = counting measure and η bijective.)

MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map gives (μ⌞S).map η = ofReal(rⁿ) • μ⌞η(S).
